newsitem.title: USA: Exxon, Union Carbide plan more catalyst plant.
newsitem.headline: Exxon, Union Carbide plan more catalyst plant.

text.p: Univation Technologies, a joint venture between Exxon Corp and Union Carbide Corp which started business today, is already looking at expanding production of metallocene catalysts, Univation chief executive Gregory McPike told a news conference.

The company is already producing enough of the catalyst to manufacture three billion pounds polyethylene a year and expects global demand for metallocene catalyst-produced polyethylene to be 4.4 billion pounds by the year 2000 out of a total global market which is projected to be in excess of 120 billion pounds of polyethylene a year.
"We have started plans for our next plant and we anticipate that the market for metallocene technology will grow rapidly over the next 15 years," McPike said.
Metallocene catalyst technology allows better control over linear low density polyethylene (LLDPE), which is used in products such as packaging, containers, garbage bags and plastic films.
The venture combines Uion Carbide's plant licensing technology with the new catalyst technology.

McPike declined to comment on the investment in the venture or projected sales for the technology which can be used in new plants in conjunction with Union Carbide's plant processing technology or in retrofitting existing plant.

Richard Sol, the venture's head of licensing marketing said that the new venture aimed to capture in excess of 50 percent of third-party new capacity, which analysts estimate at in excess of five plants a year.
Univation is also expanding the application of metallocene technology to low-pressure low density polyethylene, which will expand the range of potential end-products.
"Early metallocene products tend to be high-performance, tough materials," said Bill Fraser, head of research and development.
Union Carbide and Exxon said that one of the reasons for the formation of a joint venture was to avoid patent disputes between the two companies.
Lawsuits alleging breach of patent have dogged the technology, and Exxon and British Petroleum Co Plc have suits pending in the British and French courts.
Dow Chemical Co and Phillips Petroleum Co also have competing technologies and all are fighting to get products to market.

"Everyone who wants to produce polyethyene is going to need this product. Several companies in Europe are already talking to us about licensing," said McPike. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
